title: Headwise outlier attenuation + layer-scale annealing calibration workflow for FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a model-specific calibration and validation workflow that combines head-wise outlier attenuation and a layer-scale annealing schedule to stabilize FP8 and INT8 quant profiles on LLaMA2-70B, Mistral-7B-instruct, and Qwen-14B.

Background: Recent calibration runs show that global per-layer scales are brittle for some models due to sparse, heavy-tailed activation spikes concentrated in a small number of attention heads and feedforward dimensions. This causes downstream generation regressions for FP8 and INT8 fast paths despite acceptable mean-square errors during calibration.

Proposal: 1) Instrument a head-wise and channel-wise outlier detector in the calibration harness that computes per-head activation percentiles and kurtosis, marking heads with >99.9th percentile spikes for attenuation. 2) Apply a soft attenuation mask (headwise damping factor 0.6-0.95) during scale computation rather than hard clipping to preserve distribution shape. 3) Introduce a layer-scale annealing schedule during quant-profile extraction: start with conservative scales (larger dynamic range) for early iterations, then shrink scales over 3-5 passes using observed quantization error and generation-quality feedback. 4) Maintain an exception policy for Qwen attention patterns where per-head KV accumulation causes persistent large keys; in those cases prefer per-head asymmetric quant scales for KV caches.

Acceptance criteria: - FP8 and INT8 profiles achieve <=1.5% relative degradation on the production MMLU/LLamaEval mixes for LLaMA2-70B and Qwen-14B, and <=2.0% for Mistral-7B-instruct. - Generation quality (ROUGE-L on the summarization suite + human blind eval samples) shows no significant regressions versus baseline float runs. - CI calibration jobs pass nightly with no more than 2% failure rate across sampled models. - Integration test with Serving runtime shows stable latency within SLA for runtime-1.20 with automatic fallback to higher-precision profiles when triggers fire.

Plan & experiments: - Phase 1 (this ticket): implement headwise detection + soft attenuation + annealing controller in the calibration harness (calib/harness). Run on representative dataset rwk-v2 (mix of short chats, long context, and code). - Phase 2: run batch of 100 calibration seeds per model variant, measure distribution of scale factors and per-token quant error, collect generation metrics. - Phase 3: evaluate on the production eval set and perform small-scale customer-mirroring test on Dedicated infra. - Phase 4: roll forward profiles in canary with automatic rollback if SLA or eval regressions observed.

Instrumentation & artifacts: - Calibration config prototype: internal Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QUANT/Headwise-Attenuation-Anneal - Representative workload repo: https://git.redwood.ai/rwk/v2 - Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-harness/pull/3456 - Bench dashboard (WIP): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant/profiles-comparison

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: over-attenuation may remove useful signal and hurt rare-token accuracy. Mitigation: conservative default damping (0.85) and hold-out validation on rare-token subset. - Risk: additional compute/time for multi-pass annealing. Mitigation: early-stopping when scale changes <0.5% and parallelize passes across shards.

Rollout: Stage configs behind a feature flag (quant.head_attenuation=true) and gate default for hosted API to runtime-1.20 opt-in during initial 2-week canary.
